---
order: 4
unit: economics
title: Spending choices
node: AC9HS6K08 n1
summary: "Lots of things influence what we buy, not just what we like: how much money we have, what friends have, advertising, and what we care about (such as the environment or fairness). Noticing the influences helps you choose on purpose, and every choice still gives something up."
language: science
shape: primer
hook: "Mia picked a new drink bottle in under a minute. Was it really just because she liked it?"
---
When we buy something, lots of things push and pull on the choice. These are **influences**:

- **Money:** how much it costs, and how much you have.
- **People:** what friends and family have, use or say.
- **Advertising:** ads, packaging and displays made to catch your eye.
- **What you care about:** the environment, fairness, quality, or what your family or culture values.

You still choose. Noticing the influences helps you choose **on purpose**. And every choice gives something up: the money you spend on one thing can't buy another.

Mia and the shop are made up. Riverbend is a made-up town.

## Think first

```step
stage: predict
insight: "Committing shows whether students think a choice is 'just liking it'."
check:
  type: predict
  q: "Mia chose a $20 metal drink bottle over a $6 plastic one. Her best friend has the same metal one, she saw an ad for it last week, and she wants to stop buying plastic. Why did she choose it?"
  options: ["Several influences together: a friend, an ad and what she cares about", "Only because she liked it", "Only because it was the cheapest", "Nothing influenced her"]
  actual: "Several things pushed the same way: her friend has one, she'd seen an ad, and she cares about using less plastic. It wasn't the cheapest, so money pulled the other way."
```

## Try: sort the influences

```step
stage: run
insight: "Sorting puts names on the push and pull behind one choice."
check:
  type: sort
  q: "Sort each thing that influenced Mia's choice."
  options: ["Money", "People", "Advertising", "What she cares about"]
  items:
    - ["The metal bottle cost $14 more", "Money", "The price pulled her towards the cheaper one."]
    - ["Her best friend has the same one", "People", "Friends' choices influence ours."]
    - ["She saw an ad for it last week", "Advertising", "The ad was made to catch her eye."]
    - ["She wants to stop buying plastic", "What she cares about", "Her values about the environment."]
```

## The idea: noticing the influences

```step
stage: investigate
insight: "Seeing Nib deny any influence shows why naming influences matters."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: bug
      code: "working.txt#nib"
      text: "Click the first line where Nib's thinking goes wrong."
      answer: 3
      fault: logic
      misconception: choices-uninfluenced
      explain: "Line 3: half the class having the same shoes, and the ads everywhere, are influences. Nib still chose, but not from nowhere."
    smaller:
      check: { type: question, q: "If half your class wore the same shoes, might that affect what you notice in a shop?", options: ["Yes, it might", "No, never"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Most of us notice what friends have, even when we don't mean to."], explain: "What friends have is an influence, even when we don't notice it." }
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "Which of these is an influence from advertising?"
      options: ["A bright display at the shop door", "Having $30 to spend", "A friend's new shoes", "Wanting things that last"]
      answer: 0
      explain: "Displays are made to catch your eye. The others are money, people and what you care about."
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "Mia spends her $20 on the bottle. What does she give up?"
      options: ["The next best thing she could have bought with that $20", "Nothing, because she wanted it", "The plastic bottle she didn't buy, and everything else in the shop", "Her friend"]
      answer: 0
      explain: "Every choice gives something up: the next best thing that money could have bought."
```

## Check: before you move on

```step
stage: practise
insight: "A last sort on a new choice checks the four kinds of influence."
check:
  type: sort
  q: "Dev is choosing a phone case. Sort each influence."
  options: ["Money", "People", "Advertising", "What he cares about"]
  items:
    - ["He has $15 saved", "Money", "What he can afford."]
    - ["His brother says one brand breaks easily", "People", "Advice from family."]
    - ["An ad showed one case surviving a drop from a roof", "Advertising", "Made to make that case look tough."]
    - ["He wants one made from recycled plastic", "What he cares about", "His values about the environment."]
```

## Evaluate

```step
stage: info
check: { type: reflect, text: "I can name four kinds of influence on a spending choice, and I know that every choice gives something up." }
```

## Make: your own

```step
stage: make
insight: "Naming the influences on a made-up purchase makes the idea your own."
check: { type: reflect, text: "In my own book I chose a made-up purchase (a lunchbox, a game, a pair of shoes), wrote three influences on it, and one thing the buyer would give up. A partner read it." }
```

```teacher
summary: Students name the influences on a spending choice (money, people,
  advertising, and what they care about) and see that every choice gives
  something up. The common mistake is thinking nothing influences what we buy.
learning: name influences on a spending choice and say what the choice gives up
time: 20
timing: Think first and Try 6 min · The idea 7 min · Check 3 min · Make 4 min.
goals:
  - I can name four kinds of influence on what people buy.
  - I can spot the influences behind a choice.
  - I can say what a choice gives up.
struggle: "Students say 'I just like it'. Ask: why do you think you noticed that
  one in the first place?"
before: >
  Year 6 catch-up for AC9HS6K08 n1 (influences on consumer choices). The other
  Year 6 nodes (selling strategies, kinds of payment, strategies for informed
  choices) are left to Year 6 classes. Year 7 Scarcity and opportunity cost and
  Work, income and identity list it under what students should already know.


  "Influences" doesn't mean people can't choose freely; the point is choosing on
  purpose. Nothing asks about students' own spending; Mia, Dev and the shop are
  made up.
running:
  - "Think first: ask the 'only because she liked it' group what made her notice
    that bottle."
stuck:
  - see: A student says nothing influences them.
    ask: Where did you first see the thing you last wanted?
    fix: We still choose, but the choice doesn't come from nowhere.
stretch: Which kind of influence is hardest to notice, and why?
support: "A four-box card: Money, People, Advertising, What I care about."
leads: |
  Next: Year 7 Scarcity and opportunity cost, or Work, income and identity.
exit:
  q: Name two influences on a spending choice and what the choice gives up.
  a: "For example: a friend has one, and an ad; it gives up the next best thing
    the money could buy."
explain: >
  **Influences** on a spending choice include **money**, **people**,
  **advertising** and **what you care about**. Noticing them helps you choose on
  purpose, and every choice gives something up.
class:
  inquiry:
    q: Do you choose what you buy, or does something choose for you?
    prompts:
      - Where do you first hear about things you want?
    notes: "Aim for: lots of influences, and we still choose."
  activities:
    - at: run
      kind: activity
      title: Four corners of a choice
      minutes: 4
      do: >
        Read out Mia's four reasons. Students point to the corner for money,
        people, advertising or what she cares about.
      notes: Ask which ones pushed her towards the bottle and which pulled away.
  questions:
    - at: investigate
      title: What she gives up
      type: question
      q: Mia spends $20 on a bottle. What does she give up?
      options:
        - The next best thing that money could buy
        - Nothing
        - Everything in the shop
        - Her friend
      answer: 0
      explain: Every choice gives something up.
```
